rubric.why: A cofactor is a non-protein substance needed for enzyme activity.

rubric.why: A valid example completes the answer.

rubric.why: Churning is caused by the muscular contractions of the stomach.
rubric.description: Identifies stomach muscle contractions as the action that churns food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the muscular action in the stomach.

rubric.why: Churning mixes food with gastric juice and mechanically breaks it up.
rubric.description: States the mixing or mechanical breaking effect of churning.

modelAnswer: Churning is the mechanical mixing and breaking up of food by muscular contractions of the stomach.
It mixes the food with gastric juice.

items.followUp: Explain how transpiration helps water move from roots to leaves.

rubric.why: Transpiration pull is generated by water evaporating from the leaves.
rubric.description: Identifies water loss or evaporation from leaves as the cause of the pull.

rubric.why: The force pulls water upward through xylem from roots toward leaves.
rubric.description: Explains the upward movement of water through the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the effect and direction.

modelAnswer: Transpiration pull is the pulling force created when water evaporates from the leaves.
It pulls water upward from the roots to the leaves through the xylem.

items.followUp: State the rules for writing genus and species names in binomial nomenclature.

rubric.why: The definition must state that the scientific name has two parts, genus and species.
rubric.description: Defines binomial nomenclature as a two-word scientific name made up of genus and species.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the two-part scientific name and its genus and species components.

rubric.why: Scientific names provide a standard name used internationally.
rubric.description: States that the naming system is standard and internationally accepted.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its universal use.

rubric.why: A standard name prevents confusion caused by differing common or local names.
rubric.description: Explains that binomial nomenclature avoids confusion from common or local names.

rubric.why: The name identifies an organism and shows the genus to which it belongs.
rubric.description: States that the name identifies the organism or indicates its genus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its identification or classification value.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature is the system of giving each organism a two word scientific name: the first word is its genus and the second its species.
It provides a standard name that is used internationally.
It avoids confusion caused by different common or local names.
The two-part name identifies an organism and shows the genus to which it belongs.
